title: Afterhours compact rollout cookbook and watch slate (Mar 2026)
content:
Purpose:
This is a compact, afterhours-focused rollout cookbook for small surface-impact changes that must happen in a quiet window. It combines a tight timeline, operator cues, telemetry watchlist and a simple rollback ladder. The goal: get to production with minimal blast radius, short ops overhead, and clear handoffs for night/late shifts.

Audience:
- Release conductor on duty
- On-call SRE/Observability shift
- Small feature owner (single primary)
- Customer-facing incident lead (on-call rotation)

Scope / When to use this cookbook:
- Low-risk config flips, model variant swaps, or lightweight runtime tweaks that affect <5% of requests initially.
- Changes that can be rolled back via config toggles, routing policy, or quick instance replacement (no DB schema).
- NOT for multi-region capacity shifts or major model upgrades.

High-level timeline (compact 3.5h window):
- T-minus 45m: preflight + comms + final signoff (primary + SRE + product)
- T-minus 15m: lock deployment queue, snapshot key metrics, start live trace session
- T0: push config/model routing change to canary lane (1% traffic)
- T+5m: verify canary health signals, expand to 10% if green
- T+20m: expand to 30% and monitor for regressions
- T+45m: expand to 100% (or stop and roll back if threshold breached)
- T+60m: observe stabilization window, debrief, close runbook

Preflight checklist (45m before):
- [ ] Confirm on-call RTO window and handover contacts (SRE, infra lead, product owner)
- [ ] Post short Slack thread in #release-ops with TLDR and watch channel
- [ ] Ensure latest canary images/configs are staged and accessible with hashes
- [ ] Snapshot baseline telemetry (latency p50/p95, error rate, token cost per request, tail latency) to a short pastebin or ticket
- [ ] Wire up distributed trace session: enable ephemeral trace link and share with crew
- [ ] Confirm rollback knob (feature flag, route predicate, firewall rule id) and test it in staging
- [ ] Validate smoke tests run and pass in preflight environment (list smoke run id)
- [ ] Reserve a 60-min meeting room for post-mortem if needed

Operator run (step-by-step):
- Stage 1 (T0): Canary 1%
  - Apply routing rule to point 1% traffic to variant A (command + exact invocation shown below)
  - Wait 120s for routing propagation; watch arrival of traces
  - Check: p50 latency within 10% of baseline, error rate delta < 0.1% absolute
  - If pass: proceed to Stage 2. If fail: immediately trigger rollback knob and notify incident lead.

- Stage 2 (T+5m): Canary 10%
  - Expand to 10% using the same route patch; note commit id and timestamp
  - Run targeted synthetic requests (2 patterns: short prompt, long prompt) and confirm response shape and tokens
  - Check: p95 < baseline p95 * 1.25, tail errors not increasing, no new 5xx patterns
  - If pass: proceed to Stage 3. If marginal: hold for 15m and re-evaluate.

- Stage 3 (T+20m): Ramp to 30%
  - Expand and keep active watch; start a small sampling job to surface hallucination/regression signals (if applicable)
  - Check: quality regression metrics within acceptance thresholds, cost per token within expected band.

- Stage 4 (T+45m): Full or abort decision
  - If all green, ramp to 100% with step of 30%->60%->100% every 2–3m to avoid step shocks.
  - If not green, follow Rollback ladder.

Rollback ladder (fastest to slowest):
- 0) Emergency abort: toggle global kill switch (only if catastrophic)
- 1) Immediate route rollback to previous stable config (single command, documented below)
- 2) Scale down new variant pool to zero and reattach stable pool
- 3) Revert last config commit in control plane and redeploy stable manifest
- 4) If persistent undiagnosed issue, open incident and keep traffic throttled to safety lane (5–10%) until root cause triage complete

Telemetry watchlist (what to watch in the first 60m):
- Latency: p50, p95, p99 per region and per model route
- Errors: total 4xx/5xx counts and error pattern signatures (latency-related vs model-internal)
- Resource signals: GPU memory pressure, GPU util, OOMs, host CPU steal
- Token economics: per-request token spend and average tokens/response (spike may indicate runaway generation)
- Quality heuristics: hallucination marker count, rerank score drop, customer complaint signals (if any open channels)
- Traces: top 5 traces by duration, frequency of cache misses (KV prefix cache), cold-kv indicators

Observability quick commands (ops crib):
- Snapshot baseline (example): aws s3 cp s3://runbook-snapshots/last-24h-metrics.json ./snapshot-{{ts}}
- Toggle route (example): ./opsctl route set --route-id r-207 --variant stable --percent 100 --author maya.c
- Kill switch (example): ./opsctl emergency-stop --reason "latency surge" --author maya.c
- Rollback commit (example): git revert --no-edit 0a1b2c3 && ./deploy-manifest --env prod --tag stable

Communications script (short messages):
- Preflight post: "Starting compact afterhours rollout for [change brief]. On-call: @ravi @elena. Timeline T-45m -> T+60m. Watch: #release-ops. Rollback: route knob r-207."
- Canary pass post: "Canary 1% passed baseline checks. Expanding to 10% now. Links: traces, metrics."
- Abort post: "Abort: rolling back change due to [metric]. Rolling to stable. Incident lead: @jonah."
- Done post: "Rollout complete, stable. Summary: final p95 delta, cost delta, any notable findings. Closing runbook."

Owner responsibilities (night shift):
- Primary: execute operator run, keep notes in the ticket, call for rollback if thresholds breached
- SRE: monitor telemetry feeds and triage infra signals
- Product owner: validate qualitative checks (sanity of outputs) and approve ramp to 100%
- Comm lead: update customer channels if any degradation that affects SLAs

Post-run debrief (within 4 hours):
- Fill short template: what went well, what surprised us, telemetry deltas, and followups (who will own fixes)
- If any anomalies occurred, attach traces and top failing request ids to the ticket
- Decide if CI gating or additional unit tests are needed to prevent recurrence

Runbook notes to self / loose items:
- We should add an automated synthetic that runs long prompt + guardrail token checks during Stage 2 to catch runaway generative loops earlier.
- Investigate adding a real-time per-route cost alarm to catch sudden token spend spikes.
- Consider a smaller expansion increment for customers with strict latency SLAs (10% -> 20% -> 40%).

Appendix: Quick checklist for small ops scripts (copy into terminal before run)
- export OPS_AUTHOR=maya.c
- ./opsctl login --token-file ~/.ops_token
- ./opsctl route snapshot --route r-207 --out snapshot-{{ts}}.json
- ./opsctl route patch --route r-207 --variant candidate --percent 1

Unresolved questions:
- Who rotates the customer-facing incident lead for midnight windows by default? (proposal: current on-call + product owner).
- Should the kill-switch be reachable by SRE-only or ops lead + SRE? needs decision.

Related artifacts and links:
- Confluence: Rollout Playbooks v3 (linked above)
- Jira: RELEX-4128 (phase gate ticket for this rollout)
- PR: ops-scripts #211 (route patch helpers)
